Text_Reference: INTRODUCTION: 'Here, we describe a rapid clearing method that maintains tissue volume and preserves fluorescent signal from tracers, immunohistochemistry and genetically expressed fluorescent proteins.'

SUMMARY: 'Using ClearT or ClearT2, which are composed of formamide or formamide/polyethylene glycol, respectively, embryos, whole mounts and thick brain sections can be rapidly cleared with minimal volume changes.'

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: 'Here, we demonstrate the versatility of our method, named ClearT for neuronal and non-neuronal tissue, and compare its clarity, rapidity and tissue expansion/shrinkage to existing clearing methods.'
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: 'This modified method, named ClearT2, also requires immersion in a graded series of formamide/PEG solutions (25% formamide/10% PEG then 50% formamide/20% PEG).'

General_Description.Text: ClearT and ClearT2 are rapid tissue clearing methods that use formamide and a mixture of formamide/polyethylene glycol, respectively. These methods are designed for enhanced visualization of cell morphology and connections in neuronal and non-neuronal tissue, preserving fluorescent signals from tracers, immunohistochemistry, and genetically expressed fluorescent proteins. ClearT renders tissue transparent significantly faster than other methods like ScaleA2, with minimal volume changes, while ClearT2 maintains fluorescence better and is suitable for immunohistochemistry and genetically encoded fluorescent proteins. Both methods do not use detergents or solvents, preserving lipophilic dyes, fluorescent tracers, and immunohistochemical labeling.
Text_Reference: SUMMARY: 'We describe a clearing method for enhanced visualization of cell morphology and connections in neuronal and non-neuronal tissue. Using ClearT or ClearT2, which are composed of formamide or formamide/polyethylene glycol, respectively, embryos, whole mounts and thick brain sections can be rapidly cleared with minimal volume changes. Unlike other available clearing techniques, these methods do not use detergents or solvents, and thus preserve lipophilic dyes, fluorescent tracers and immunohistochemical labeling, as well as fluorescent-protein labeling.'

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: 'ClearT is a rapid tissue clearing method... The ClearT procedure rendered embryonic brains as transparent as with ScaleA2, but did so significantly faster (1 day versus 14 days)... ClearT does not lead to volume changes... ClearT is incompatible with immunohistochemistry and genetically encoded fluorescence proteins... ClearT2 clears tissue with fluorescent protein and with immunohistochemical label... ClearT2 clears specimens while effectively maintaining the fluorescent signal of genetically encoded proteins, immunohistochemistry labeling, and dye tracers such as DiI and CTB... ClearT and ClearT2 provide several advantages over other available clearing methods... Clearing time for thick sections, whole brains or embryos is significantly faster than with ScaleA2 or BABB... ClearT and ClearT2 produce minimal tissue volume changes... Most importantly, our methods maintain DiI- and CTB-labeling in axons, unlike ScaleA2 and BABB... ClearT and ClearT2 successfully clear postnatal and adult brain and other tissues. ClearT2 provides a final important advantage over ScaleA2 and BABB, in that it can clear immunolabeled tissue.'

Tissue_Types.Text4: Intact embryos, embryonic and postnatal dissected heads, brains, and thick (up to 1000 μm) brain sections.
Text4_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION, ClearT is a rapid tissue clearing method: 'Intact embryos, embryonic and postnatal dissected heads, brains, and thick (up to 1000 μm) brain sections, were fixed and sequentially immersed in graded concentrations of formamide (Table 1A, Fig. 1A).'

Time_Consumption.Text1: The ClearT procedure rendered embryonic brains as transparent as with ScaleA2, but did so significantly faster (1 day versus 14 days).
Text1_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION section: 'The ClearT procedure rendered embryonic brains as transparent as with ScaleA2, but did so significantly faster (1 day versus 14 days).' Fig. 1B.

Time_Consumption.Text2: ClearT2 clears tissue with fluorescent protein and with immunohistochemical label within 1 or 2 days, with sections treated with ClearT2 slightly larger than pre-cleared sections.
Text2_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION section: 'Sections treated with ClearT2 for 1 or 2 days were slightly larger than pre-cleared sections, but these changes were significantly less than with ScaleA2.'

Time_Consumption.Text3: ClearT and ClearT2 provide improved clearing of embryonic and adult neuronal and non-neuronal tissue for viewing fluorescent labeling of cells and fiber tracts by high-resolution optical imaging, with clearing time for thick sections, whole brains or embryos significantly faster than with ScaleA2 or BABB.
Text3_Reference: ClearT and ClearT2 are solvent- and detergent-free rapid tissue clearing methods section: 'Clearing time for thick sections, whole brains or embryos is significantly faster than with ScaleA2 or BABB.'

Time_Consumption.Text4: Fixed whole embryos (E14.5) and dissected postnatal brains (P0) were cleared overnight. The grid is visible through tissue cleared by ClearT.

Tissue_Deformation.Text1: Completely cleared postnatal day 0 (P0) brain sections were similar to their original size (before clearing=1.0±0 versus ClearT=1.04±0.02, not significant, n=6 sections).
Text1_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION section, 'ClearT is a rapid tissue clearing method': 'Completely cleared postnatal day 0 (P0) brain sections were similar to their original size...'

Tissue_Deformation.Text2: Even after prolonged treatment with ClearT, sample volume only increased slightly, significantly less than in ScaleA2 [1 day, ClearT=1.33±0.09 versus ScaleA2=1.81±0.05, P<0.01; 2 days, ClearT=1.27±0.09 versus ScaleA2=1.83±0.06, P<0.01, n=5 (ClearT), 4 (ScaleA2) sections].
Text2_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION section, 'ClearT is a rapid tissue clearing method': 'Even after prolonged treatment with ClearT, sample volume only increased slightly...'

Tissue_Deformation.Text3: ClearT2 induced robust transparency of thick P0 brain sections without volume changes (before clearing=1.0 versus ClearT2=0.98±0.02, n=6, not significant).
Text3_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION section, 'ClearT2 clears tissue with fluorescent protein and with immunohistochemical label': 'ClearT2 induced robust transparency of thick P0 brain sections without volume changes...'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text1: ClearT preserves DiI labeling of retinal axons in the optic nerve and chiasm, but treatment with either ScaleA2 or BABB degraded the fluorescent signal.
Text1_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION, Visualization of DiI- or CTB-labeled axons in tissue cleared with ClearT: 'DiI labeling of retinal axons in the optic nerve and chiasm was preserved after treatment with ClearT, but treatment with either ScaleA2 or BABB degraded the fluorescent signal.'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text2: CTB labeling was preserved after ClearT and BABB treatments, but BABB reduced tissue size by half, while labeling was diffuse following ScaleA2 treatment.
Text2_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION, Visualization of DiI- or CTB-labeled axons in tissue cleared with ClearT: 'CTB labeling was preserved after ClearT and BABB treatments, but BABB reduced tissue size by half, while labeling was diffuse following ScaleA2 treatment.'

Our original ClearT protocol diminished green fluorescent protein (GFP) intensity...ClearT2 clears specimens while effectively maintaining the fluorescent signal of genetically encoded proteins, immunohistochemistry labeling, and dye tracers such as DiI and CTB.'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text4: ClearT2 successfully preserved RC2 immunolabeling, unlike ClearT and ScaleA2 which disrupted RC2 immunolabeling, and BABB which produced labeling artifacts.
Text4_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION, ClearT2 clears tissue with fluorescent protein and with immunohistochemical label: 'ClearT and ScaleA2 disrupted RC2 immunolabeling, and BABB maintained fluorescent signal but produced labeling artifacts...ClearT2 successfully preserved immunolabeling.'

Text5_Reference: MATERIALS AND METHODS, Immunohistochemistry: 'Mouse monoclonal anti-RC2 (IgM) antibody (Developmental Hybridoma Bank)(1:4) and mouse monoclonal anti-neurofilament (IgG) antibody (2H3) (a gift from T. Jessell and S. Morton, Columbia University, NY, USA) (1:5) were incubated in 1% BSA/1% Tween in PBS overnight at 4°C. After washes with 1% Tween in PBS, Cy3-conjugated anti-mouse IgM and Cy5conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) secondary antibodies (Jackson) were applied, incubated in 1% BSA/1% Tween in PBS overnight at 4°C.'

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION, ClearT2 clears tissue with fluorescent protein and with immunohistochemical label: 'ClearT and ScaleA2 disrupted RC2 immunolabeling, and BABB maintained fluorescent signal but produced labeling artifacts in bone and cell nuclei that should not express RC2. As ClearT2 successfully preserved immunolabeling (supplementary material Fig. S5A-E), we applied it to 200 μm RC2-immunolabeled vibratome sections of the optic chiasm at E14.5 (Fig. 3D).'

Text6_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION, Visualization of DiI- or CTB-labeled axons in tissue cleared with ClearT: 'To test the compatibility of CTB with ClearT, we anterogradely labeled each eye of P5 pups with CTB conjugated to either Alexa Fluor 488 or 594. CTB labeling was preserved after ClearT and BABB treatments, but BABB reduced tissue size by half (before clearing=1±0 versus cleared=0.50±0.02, P<0.05, n=4 sections), while labeling was diffuse following ScaleA2 treatment (supplementary material Fig. S2B).'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text8: Streptavidin-Alexa Fluor 647 and CTB conjugated to Alexa Fluor 594 are compatible with ClearT2.

Text9_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION, ClearT2 clears tissue with fluorescent protein and with immunohistochemical label: 'After clearing thick hippocampal sections with ClearT2, Thy1-GFP+ neurons were visible deeper within the granule cell layer (Fig. 3C, top) and details of GFP+ pyramidal neuron dendrites in the CA1 region were more distinct than without clearing (Fig. 3C, bottom).'

Preservation_Stability.Text1: Although formamide is not harmful to tissue in the short term, it is unsuitable for long-term tissue storage. Therefore, we transferred samples treated with ClearT into PBS, where they became opaque within 30 minutes and could be safely stored for at least 1 month.

Application.Text5: ClearT2 method enhances the resolution and visibility of fluorescent labels in thick brain sections with multiple fluorescent labels, preserving both CTB and biocytin labeling.
Text5_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION section, 'ClearT2 clears tissue with fluorescent protein and with immunohistochemical label': 'After applying ClearT2 to a thick brain section with CTB-labeled dLGN, a biocytin-filled relay neuron was visualized more deeply and at higher resolution than before clearing, with both labels successfully maintained.'

Application.Text6: ClearT2 method is applicable to adult and non-neuronal tissue, preserving fluorescent protein expression in various tissues including the cerebral cortex and small intestine.
Text6_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION section, 'ClearT2 clears tissue with fluorescent protein and with immunohistochemical label': 'To determine whether ClearT2 could be applied to adult or non-neuronal tissue, we used Tcf/Lef:H2B-GFP mice... H2B-GFP nuclear labeling in neurons of the cerebral cortex, cells within the granule cell and molecular layers of the hippocampus, progenitor cells of the small intestine and satellite cells of skeletal muscle were more apparent after clearing with ClearT2.'

Application.Text7: ClearT2 method facilitates visualization of immunohistochemical labeling in thick tissue sections, allowing deeper observation of labeled structures.
Text7_Reference: RESULTS AND DISCUSSION section, 'ClearT2 clears tissue with fluorescent protein and with immunohistochemical label': 'RC2+ glial processes were visible as deep as ~120 μm in cleared tissue, twice as deep as in pre-cleared tissue.'

Application.Text8: Finally, ClearT2 treatment of whole mouse embryos immunostained with an antibody to neurofilament (NF) provided a complete view of axon tracts and arbors in the CNS and PNS in distal appendages (Fig. 3E).
